name: CA-47
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by six points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Dave Min holds a large financial advantage ($1.9M vs $0.1M cash on hand)
Prediction markets price Min's win chances near 97%
No public general-election polling is available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Min: a D+6 district, incumbency, a roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge, and markets pricing his win probability around 97%. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: A late surge in Republican outside spending or an unexpectedly favorable national environment could narrow the margin, though an upset remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dave Min, a first-term Democratic incumbent, defends a Southern California district that voted about six points more Democratic than the country in recent baseline measures. He advanced to the general election and faces Republican Jenny Le Roux, a first-time candidate with modest resources. Min has raised about $3.4 million and holds $1.9 million on hand, while Le Roux has raised under $400,000 with roughly $130,000 available, and outside spending has been negligible on both sides.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district lean, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Min's chances near 97 percent. The combined evidence points to a comfortable double-digit Democratic win, with only modest residual uncertainty from the absence of polling.
